texts.full_text: There is growing concern, even among developed countries, about the increasing incidence of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis (MDR-Tb). Results are reported from a study investigating ofloxacin used in the treatment of 57 patients with MDR-TB. Patients received ofloxacin 400 mg/day as well as three other sensitive anti-TB drugs based on susceptibility tests. The results showed that after 12 months, 67% of patients had a response to the treatment regimen, including sputum conversion and improvement. The study highlights the potential effectiveness of using ofloxacin in combination with other anti-tuberculosis medications for treating MDR-TB cases, offering new hope for managing this challenging condition in resource-limited settings like Indonesia, where access to more advanced or expensive treatments may be restricted due to constraints.
